q.e: The exponent says how many times the base is multiplied by itself: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32 (not 2 × 5).
(−3) × (−3) × (−3): the first two give +9, and 9 × (−3) = −27. An odd power of a negative number stays negative.
A power of 10 is 1 followed by that many zeros: 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10000.
5³ ÷ 5³ = 1 (anything divided by itself), and by the division law it is also 5³⁻³ = 5⁰. So 5⁰ must be 1.
(2×2×2) × (2×2×2×2) is seven 2s multiplied, so add the exponents: 3 + 4 = 7.
Two of the six 7s on top cancel with the two below, leaving four: subtract the exponents, 6 − 2 = 4.
Ten negatives multiply in five pairs, and each pair gives +1. An even power of −1 is always 1.

q.t: In 6⁹, which number is the base?
q.e: The base is the number being multiplied (6); the exponent (9) tells how many times.
(2/3) × (2/3): square the top AND the bottom, 2²/3² = 4/9.
(2³)⁴ means 2³ × 2³ × 2³ × 2³ — four groups of three 2s = twelve 2s. Multiply the exponents: 3 × 4 = 12.
(3×3) × (5×5) can be regrouped as (3×5) × (3×5) = 15². Same exponent → multiply the bases.
Same base, so add exponents: (−2)⁸. An even power is positive: 2⁸ = 256.
4⁵ ÷ 4³ = 4². Then 4² × 4¹ = 4³ = 64. A lone 4 has exponent 1.
Standard form has one non-zero digit before the point. The point moves 5 places left (from the end to after the 3), so × 10⁵.
(5²)³ = 5⁶. Then 5⁶ ÷ 5⁴ = 5² = 25.

q.t: Write 72 as a product of powers of its prime factors.
q.e: 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 2³ × 3². (8 × 9 is correct in value, but 8 and 9 are not prime.)
Cube the top and the bottom: 3³/4³ = 27/64.
Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1, so this is 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.
2⁵ = 32 and 5² = 25. Swapping base and exponent changes the value.
Keep doubling: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 — that is six 2s, so x = 6.
Write 4 = 2² and 32 = 2⁵. Top: 2⁷ × 3⁴. Bottom: 2⁵ × 3². Subtract exponents: 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36.
(−4)³ = −64, 5² = 25, (−1)⁷ = −1. Two negative factors make a positive: 64 × 25 = 1600.
× 10⁶ moves the point 6 places right: 6.02 → 6020000 (written 60,20,000).
243 = 3⁵. Same base, so the exponents are equal: x + 2 = 5, giving x = 3.
3/2 is the reciprocal of 2/3, so each (3/2) cancels one (2/3). Two cancel, leaving (2/3)² = 4/9.
In standard form, compare the powers of 10 first. 10¹² is ten thousand times bigger than 10⁸.
10⁶ ÷ 10³ = 10³ (subtract). Then 10³ × 10² = 10⁵ (add).

q.t: Write 432 as a product of powers of prime factors.

q.e: Same base: add the exponents on the left, 4 + 5 = 9. So 3x = 9 and x = 3.
Every zero power is 1: (1 + 1) × 1 − 1 = 1.
Break into primes. Top: 12⁴ = 2⁸·3⁴, 9³ = 3⁶, 4 = 2² → 2¹⁰·3¹⁰. Bottom: 6³ = 2³·3³, 8² = 2⁶, 27 = 3³ → 2⁹·3⁶. Result 2¹ × 3⁴ = 162.
9 = 3², so the left side is 3²⁺ˣ. Then 2 + x = 7 and x = 5.

q.t: Which of these is the largest?
q.e: Make every exponent 20: 3⁴⁰ = (3²)²⁰ = 9²⁰ and 2⁶⁰ = (2³)²⁰ = 8²⁰. With equal exponents the biggest base wins: 9 > 8 > 5 > 4.

q.t: The Sun is about 1.5 × 10⁸ km from Earth and light travels 3 × 10⁵ km every second. About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
q.e: Time = distance ÷ speed = (1.5 ÷ 3) × 10⁸⁻⁵ = 0.5 × 10³ = 500 seconds (about 8 minutes).
Odd powers of −1 are −1, even powers are +1: −1 + 1 − 1 = −1.

q.t: What is the units digit of 2¹⁵?
q.e: The last digits of powers of 2 repeat every four: 2, 4, 8, 6. 15 = 4 × 3 + 3, so it is the 3rd in the cycle: 8.

q.t: If a = 2 and b = 3, find (aᵇ + bᵃ) × aᵃ.

q.e: You can only add when the powers match: 54000 + 6000 = 60000 = 6 × 10⁴. Exponents are NOT added in addition.
